0|aae0777f1e8224b4fbb78b2c692060852ee750c8|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"KVM: PPC: Book3S HV: Split HPT allocation from activation
Currently
column2: kvmppc_alloc_hpt() both allocates a new hashed page table (HPT)

column1: and sets it up as the active page table for a VM.  For the upcoming HPT
resize implementation we're going to want to allocate HPTs separately from
activating them.
So
column2: split the allocation itself out into kvmppc_allocate_hpt() and perform

column1: the activation with a new kvmppc_set_hpt() function.  Likewise we split
kvmppc_free_hpt()
which unsets it as an active HPT
We also move the logic to fall back to smaller HPT sizes if the first try
fails into the single caller which used that behaviour
kvmppc_hv_setup_htab_rma().  This introduces a slight semantic change
that previously if the initial attempt at CMA allocation failed
fall back to attempting smaller sizes with the page allocator.  Now
try first CMA
column2: then the page allocator at each size.  As far as I can tell

column1: this change should be harmless.
To match
column2: we make kvmppc_free_hpt() just free the actual HPT itself.  The

column1: call to kvmppc_free_lpid() that was there
column2: we move to the single caller.
